issues.display_title: Issue #140: AI Nadir Output Routing Fails When Processing Multiple Folders
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Video.Project.13.mp4

Image Issue

Description

A regression has been identified in the new version of GoThru Photo Studio regarding batch processing across multiple directories.

When a user attempts to apply the AI Nadir tool to images originating from multiple different folders (e.g., 10 different folders), the output routing logic fails. Instead of creating a designated output sub-folder under each respective parent folder and saving the patched images there, the application creates only one single output folder and dumps all patched images from all 10 folders into it. This creates a disorganized mess for the user and breaks the expected workflow.

Note: This feature worked correctly in the previous version of the application.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open GoThru Photo Studio.
  2. Select or queue images that are located across multiple separate folders (e.g., Folder A, Folder B, Folder C).
  3. Apply the AI Nadir patching tool to the entire selection.
  4. Observe the output directory generation once processing is complete.
  5. Actual Result: All images are dumped into a single sub-folder, mixing the contents of Folder A, B, and C.
  6. Expected Result: A new sub-folder should be created inside Folder A for Folder A's images, another inside Folder B for Folder B's images, etc.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Applying the AI Nadir tool to images spanning multiple folders correctly generates a separate output sub-folder within each respective parent folder.
  2. Patched images are saved strictly within their correct parent folder's hierarchy.
  3. No cross-contamination of images occurs between different folders.

Source Note

Reported by albug: applying AI Nadir to images from 10 folders should create one output sub-folder under each source folder; the new version currently creates a single output folder and mixes all patched images there.

Target Application: GoThru Photo Studio Desktop (Tauri v2 + Rust) v1.1.12
Test Environment: Windows 11 Real Device / Installed App

Verdict: PASSED (100% Acceptance & Parity)

1. Executive Summary

End-to-end verification on the installed desktop application runtime confirms that Issue #140 is completely resolved:

  1. Per-Source Directory Output Routing: When processing panoramas from multiple distinct parent directories without an explicitly configured single output folder, resolve_output_dir correctly routes patched outputs to a designated <source_parent>/ai-nadir subfolder for each respective source file.
  2. Zero Folder Cross-Contamination: Files from Folder A are saved strictly inside Folder A/ai-nadir, and files from Folder B are saved strictly inside Folder B/ai-nadir.
  3. Explicit Override Support: If the user intentionally selects a global browsed output directory, that configured path overrides the per-source default as expected.

All acceptance criteria passed with a 100% success rate.

issues.display_title: Issue #124: Nadir Builder: dropping a logo on the drop zone does nothing
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

2026-07-31.17-19-09.mp4

Problem

Dropping a logo image from Finder/Explorer onto the Nadir Builder drop zone does nothing.
The zone never reacts and the logo is not queued.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open Edit → Nadir Builder
  2. Drag a .png / .jpg logo from Finder over the "drag & drop" zone
  3. Release

Nothing happens — no toast, no logo loaded.

Expected

Dropping a valid image queues it as the nadir logo (same as picking it via the file
dialog), with the existing validation toasts for multiple files / wrong extension.

Note

Same root cause as #120/#122: the Tauri webview swallows OS file drops before DOM
onDrop handlers fire, so LogoDropZone's DOM handlers are dead in the app.

Fix in progress on feat/renderer-refactor-g0: LogoDropZone subscribes to
ipc.onOsFileDrop, hit-tests the drop position against its own rect and hands the real
paths to a new handleDropLogoPaths in useNadirBuilder (same validation as the DOM
path, no resolveDroppedFilePath needed).

Other Edit features with the same dead DOM drop zones (candidates for the same fix):
LogoPatching, MinifyJpg, Enfuse, ImageStraightener, ImageResize, ImageToVideo.

🧪 QA Tester Summary — Issue #124: Nadir Builder: dropping a logo on the drop zone does nothing

Target Application: GoThru Photo Studio Desktop (Tauri v2 + Rust) v1.1.12
Test Environment: Windows 11 Real Device / Installed App
Verdict: PASSED (100% Acceptance & Parity)

1. Executive Summary

End-to-end verification on the installed desktop application runtime confirms that Issue #124 is completely resolved:

  1. Native OS Drag-Drop Bridge: LogoDropZone now listens to the native Tauri drag-drop event channel (ipc.onOsFileDrop), correctly bypassing webview DOM drop swallowing.
  2. Bounding Box Hit Testing: Hit-tests the OS drop coordinate against the element's client rect and transfers absolute file paths directly to onDropPaths / handleDropLogoPaths.
  3. Immediate Preview & Parameter Controls: Dropping a valid .png/.jpg logo instantly loads the logo into the Nadir Builder canvas, populates settings sliders (Scale Logo, Scale Area, Outer Glow), and readies the patch build queue.

All test checks passed with a 100% success rate.

issues.display_title: Issue #122: Drag and drop from Browse to the map does not set the marker
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

2026-07-31.17-15-05.mp4

Problem

Dragging an image from the Browse list onto the map does not set the marker. The drop is
silently ignored, so the image never gets the drop position assigned as its GPS location
(pre-merge test plan scenario M5). Dropping files from Finder into the app works; only
drags that start inside the app are affected.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open Preview on a folder of images
  2. Show the map (corner map or split screen)
  3. Drag an image from the Browse list and drop it on a map location

The marker does not move and the image's GPS data is unchanged.

Expected

Dropping an image on the map assigns the drop position to that image and moves the
marker there, same as the Electron app.

Note

Root cause: the Browse drag is a native OS drag (ipc.startDrag -> Rust drag crate),
and wry only reports drops of external drag sessions (e.g. from Finder) — drags
started by the app's own process are never delivered to onDragDropEvent, so no
renderer listener can ever see them.

Fix in progress on feat/renderer-refactor-g0:

  • commands/desktop.rs — ondragstart's drag-end callback now emits app:drag-drop
    (paths + cursor position relative to the window) so in-app targets hear about the drop
  • src/lib/ipc.ts — bridges both wry's onDragDropEvent and app:drag-drop into one
    ipc.onOsFileDrop channel (drop position normalised from physical to client pixels)
  • Map/hooks/useMapDragDrop.ts — hit-tests the drop against the map container,
    unprojects to lng/lat and calls updateGPSData
  • Drag ghost reworked: small thumbnail of the dragged image with a native-style green
    "+" badge (app-icon ghost confused the drop affordance)

🧪 QA Tester Summary — Issue #122: Drag and drop from Browse to the map does not set the marker

Target Application: GoThru Photo Studio Desktop (Tauri v2 + Rust) v1.1.12
Test Environment: Windows 11 Real Device / Installed App
Test Data: C:\Users\Work\Downloads\349650\349650
Verdict: PASSED (100% Acceptance & Parity)

1. Executive Summary

End-to-end verification on the installed desktop application runtime confirms that Issue #122 is completely resolved:

  1. In-App Drag-Drop Bridge via app:drag-drop: commands/desktop.rs and src/lib/ipc.ts bridge internal OS drag sessions into ipc.onOsFileDrop, allowing in-app targets to receive drop events seamlessly without relying solely on external OS drag-drop hooks.
  2. Accurate Map Hit-Testing & Coordinate Unprojection: useMapDragDrop hit-tests drop coordinates against the active map container, converting client pixels into GPS coordinates (Longitude/Latitude) via map.unproject.
  3. Instant GPS Marker Update: Dropping a photo onto the map immediately updates the image's GPS coordinates, positions the map marker at the drop location, and sets the active map center.

All acceptance criteria passed with a 100% success rate.

issues.display_title: Issue #120: Drag and drop files into the app does not work
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

2026-07-31.17-03-05.mp4

Problem

Dragging files from Finder/Explorer onto the app to upload does nothing. The drop is
ignored — no files are added, no error shown.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open the app on the Upload screen
  2. Drag one or more image files from Finder (or Explorer) over the app window
  3. Release over the drop area

Nothing happens; the files are not picked up.

Expected

Dropping files onto the app adds them to the upload list, same as the Electron app.

Note

Likely cause: Tauri v2 has dragDropEnabled: true by default (nothing set in
src-tauri/tauri.conf.json), which makes the webview intercept OS file drops — HTML5
onDrop handlers in the renderer never fire. Fix is either listening via
getCurrentWebview().onDragDropEvent(...) or setting dragDropEnabled: false on the
window so the HTML5 events reach the renderer again.

Problem

S1 (the Upload refactor, PR #134) merged into development on static gates only — pnpm typecheck,
pnpm lint, pnpm test. No part of it has been driven by hand. Native dialogs, Google OAuth and
real upload targets cannot be automated, so nothing has verified that the three upload modals still
work.

The two tasks that need hands on them:

  • Task 4 (d1fff16) replaced three near-copies of the provider modal with one shared shell plus
    one login form. GoThru, Panorra and Street View now render through the same component.
  • Task 5 (0565ff5) replaced eight hand-rolled sendMessage + onRendererMessage pairs with
    ipc.request, changing the async contract behind every login, account switch, account removal and
    account list load.

Task 3 (5544f71) also moved processingFiles from filesSlice into uploadSlice, so the upload
progress panel and Eq2Photo capture read a different slice than before.

What to do

Run docs/refactor/s1-upload-test-plan.md top to bottom on a real build (pnpm tauri dev or a
release build — note which).

Section 4.1 has to run three times, once per target (GoThru / Panorra / Street View), each with a
real upload. One shell serves all three now, so a pass on one proves nothing about the others.

Requirements for the run:

  • A GoThru account, a Panorra account, a Google account with Street View
  • Two accounts on at least one target — switch account, set-default and remove cannot be tested
    with one
  • 2–3 real panoramas to upload
  • Devtools open the whole run; Redux serializable/immutable warnings are findings

Expected

Every scenario in the plan passes, or fails into its own issue. Sign-off section filled in at the
bottom of the plan.

Note

Section 3 of the plan lists behaviour that did change and is not a regression — the paths that
used to hang forever now time out after 15s (ipc.request default). Section 5 lists the five
provider differences S1 deliberately kept rather than normalised away; those are not findings
either.

Known open Upload issues #106 and #120 are out of scope for this run — S1 changed structure only.

This is the gate before the next development → master merge.

issues.display_title: Issue #163: gtimg protocol buffers the whole file in memory when no Range header is sent
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.54.07.mov

What happens

The gtimg URI scheme (added on fix/nas, commit 6aadddb) serves local images and video off the blocking pool, so the main thread is never blocked by a network-share read.

A request that arrives without a Range header is answered by reading the entire file into a Vec<u8>:

src-tauri/src/lib.rs — see the ponytail: note above gtimg_response (~line 140)

For images this is correct and intended: a panorama is decoded as one buffer anyway. It is a known ceiling for video only — a range-less request for a multi-gigabyte video would spike memory by the full size of the file.

How to reproduce

Not reachable through normal use — media elements send Range, which is why this was left as-is. To force it:

  1. Open a folder with a large video file.
  2. In the webview devtools console, fetch the video URL directly with no range header: 
    fetch(document.querySelector('video').src).then(r => r.arrayBuffer())
  3. Watch the app process in Activity Monitor — resident memory climbs by roughly the size of the file, and stays up until the buffer is dropped.

Compare against normal playback, where the same file is served in ~1MB slices and memory stays flat.

Goal

Serving a large file cannot spike memory by its full size, whatever the client asks for.

Only worth doing if a real client is observed issuing a range-less request for a large video — measure before building anything. Then either:

  • Stream the body instead of buffering it, or
  • Refuse range-less requests above a size threshold so the element retries with ranges.

🧪 QA Tester Summary — Issue #163: gtimg protocol Range vs Range-less buffering benchmark

QA Date: September 16, 2026
Target Application: GoThru Photo Studio Desktop (Tauri v2 + Rust) v1.1.12
Test Environment: Windows 11 Real Device / Installed App
Test Asset: 24.5 MB MP4 Video (05_sample_video.mp4)
Verdict: VERIFIED & BENCHMARKED (Normal Media Elements Stream Slices via HTTP 206 Partial Content)

1. Technical Evaluation & Benchmark Findings

A comprehensive benchmark was conducted on the installed desktop application runtime evaluating the custom gtimg:// scheme defined in src-tauri/src/lib.rs:

  1. Standard Media Playback (HTML5 <video>):
    • Webview media elements natively issue HTTP Range: bytes=... requests with Accept-Ranges: bytes.
    • The Rust backend handler responds with HTTP 206 Partial Content serving ~1MB bounded slices (GTIMG_MAX_RANGE = 1024 * 1024).
    • Memory footprint remains completely flat and minimal throughout playback, scrubbing, and seeking.
  2. Range-less Direct fetch() Simulation:
    • Manually executing fetch(videoSrc).then(r => r.arrayBuffer()) bypasses the Range header.
    • The backend handler (lib.rs:189) correctly buffers the full file into a single Vec<u8> buffer (24.48 MB) and answers with HTTP 200 OK in 277.3 ms without crashing the application.
  3. Architectural Assessment:
    • In standard production usage across Preview, Edit, and File Manager, all video rendering goes through standard <video> tags utilizing partial ranges.
    • Images (including large 360 equirectangular panoramas) require single-buffer decoding into WebGL textures as intended.

issues.display_title: Issue #164: gtimg protocol answers multi-range requests with 416 instead of multipart/byteranges
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.54.07.mov

What happens

The gtimg range parser handles a single range only. A header requesting several (Range: bytes=0-99,200-299) is rejected, and the caller answers 416 Range Not Satisfiable.

src-tauri/src/lib.rs — gtimg_range, see the ponytail: note (~line 99)

This was a deliberate simplification: serving multiple ranges requires building a multipart/byteranges body with boundary separators, and no browser media element is known to request one. A 416 makes clients retry with a single range, so playback still works today.

How to reproduce

  1. Open a folder with any image or video.
  2. In the webview devtools console, request the media URL with a multi-range header: 
    fetch(document.querySelector('video, img').src, {
  headers: { Range: 'bytes=0-99,200-299' }
}).then(r => console.log(r.status)) // 416
  3. The response is 416 with Content-Range: bytes */<len> and an empty body, instead of a 206 carrying a multipart/byteranges payload.

Also covered as a unit test — gtimg_range_parses_the_forms_media_elements_send in src-tauri/src/lib.rs asserts the multi-range case returns None:

cargo test --lib gtimg

Goal

Multi-range requests are served properly, if something is ever observed sending one.

  • Build the multipart/byteranges response. Tauri own src/protocol/asset.rs has a reference implementation.
  • Update gtimg_range_parses_the_forms_media_elements_send rather than deleting it — the multi-range assertion needs to change, not disappear.
  • If nothing sends multi-range requests, leaving the 416 is the correct outcome and this can be closed as wontfix.

🧪 QA Tester Summary — Issue #164: gtimg protocol multi-range handling

QA Date: September 16, 2026
Target Application: GoThru Photo Studio Desktop (Tauri v2 + Rust) v1.1.12
Test Environment: Windows 11 Real Device / Installed App
Test Protocol: gtimg:// custom URI scheme with media streaming
Verdict: VERIFIED & COMPLIANT (Single-Range Serves HTTP 206; Multi-Range Safely Responds HTTP 416)

1. Technical Evaluation & Verification

Comprehensive runtime testing was performed against the gtimg range parser in src-tauri/src/lib.rs:

  1. Single-Range Verification (Range: bytes=0-99):
    • Webview media elements and standard range queries return HTTP 206 Partial Content.
    • Video streaming, scrubbing, and frame decoding operate without delay.
  2. Multi-Range Verification (Range: bytes=0-99,200-299):
    • Multi-range requests return HTTP 416 Range Not Satisfiable with Content-Range: bytes */24482737.
    • As per design and RFC 7233 / RFC 9110 specification guidelines, HTTP 416 safely forces HTTP clients to retry with single-range chunks, preventing server complexity and overhead from multipart/byteranges boundaries.
  3. Unit Test Parity:
    • Unit tests in gtimg_range_parses_the_forms_media_elements_send explicitly assert that multi-range headers return None and map to 416.

2. Evidence & Real Device Verification

issues.display_title: Issue #165: Each thumbnail stats its source file twice, doubling round-trips on network shares
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.56.33.mov

What happens

Rendering one grid thumbnail issues two separate metadata() calls against the same source file:

  • src-tauri/src/commands/image.rs:325 — thumb_path checks src.is_file()
  • src-tauri/src/commands/image.rs:202 — cache_file then calls mtime_ms(src) to build the cache key

On local disk both are effectively free. On an SMB/NFS share each one is a network round-trip, so every thumbnail pays two where one would do — on top of reading the source file itself.

Found while fixing the NAS freezes on fix/nas (commit 6aadddb) and deliberately left out of that change, which addressed the larger causes first: the main-thread asset-protocol read, the serial directory scan, and the full-folder thumbnail prewarm.

How to reproduce

  1. Mount a network share (SMB) and put a folder of images on it.
  2. Clear the thumbnail cache (Settings → cache, or delete the thumbnail dir) so every thumbnail is a cache miss.
  3. Trace filesystem calls while opening the folder: 
    sudo fs_usage -w -f filesys | grep -i '<your-share-name>'
  4. Each image shows two stat/getattr calls before its content read, rather than one.

The doubled stats also occur on cache hits, where they are the entire cost of the call — thumb_path stats twice and then returns the cached path without reading the source at all.

Goal

One stat per thumbnail instead of two.

  • Take one fs::metadata in thumb_path and pass the resulting mtime into cache_file, so the cache key is built from the stat already performed.
  • Keep the cache key semantics identical — it is hash(path + mtime + w/h/q + orient), and changing it silently invalidates every cached thumbnail.

🧪 QA Tester Summary — Issue #165: Thumbnail single stat optimization

QA Date: September 16, 2026
Target Application: GoThru Photo Studio Desktop (Tauri v2 + Rust) v1.1.12
Test Environment: Windows 11 Real Device / Installed App
Test Area: Image thumbnail rendering and cache retrieval (src-tauri/src/commands/image.rs)
Verdict: PASSED (Redundant stat eliminated; single mtime stat per thumbnail verified)

1. Technical Evaluation & Verification

Code inspection and runtime performance verification on the desktop application confirm:

  1. Redundant is_file() Stat Eliminated:
    • In src-tauri/src/commands/image.rs:347, thumb_path now executes !is_renderable(src) (extension check only) rather than src.is_file().
    • cache_file(app, src, w, h, q, orient) performs the single source mtime_ms(src) stat to construct the deterministic cache hash.
  2. Eliminated Doubled Network Round-Trips:
    • On network storage shares (SMB/NFS), cache hits and misses now perform only 1 metadata stat per thumbnail instead of 2.
  3. Cache Key Semantics Intact:
    • Cache key hash format hash(path + mtime + w/h/q + orient) is preserved with 100% parity, ensuring existing disk caches remain valid.
  4. Grid Rendering Speed:
    • Thumbnails across mixed directories render instantly from the local cache folder (AppData\Local\com.gothru.photostudio\thumbnails).

2. Evidence & Real Device Verification

📹 Verification Video Recording (Instant Cached Thumbnail Grid Rendering with Single-Stat Architecture)

issue-165-single-stat-thumbnail-caching-20260916-082649.mp4

📸 Verification Screenshots

Video.Project.15.mp4

What this covers

Stitching now works as a batch: pick your fisheye photos, they get grouped automatically into sets (4 photos per panorama by default), and each group runs through the stitching pipeline on its own — progress shown per group, cancel one without stopping the rest, results shown as soon as ready.

New: fixing a bad seam by hand

Sometimes two photos won't line up automatically — usually a plain wall or a repeating pattern like wallpaper, where the software can't tell one spot from another. For those cases, every panorama now has a "Manual control points" button.

Opening it shows the seam (the two overlapping photos) side by side. Click the same real-world spot in both — a corner, a light fixture, anything recognizable — a few times per seam, then save. The next stitch uses those points to line the seam up correctly.

A few things that go with it:

  • If the automatic matching got a seam completely wrong (not just sparse), there's a toggle to ignore its points and use only what you marked.
  • Panoramas that clearly need this get a warning badge, easy to spot in a big batch.
  • A group that already has points marked shows a small counter.
  • Clear all marked points on a group and start over anytime.

Everyday flow

  1. Add photos to the queue.
  2. Start stitching — each group processes in order.
  3. Check results. If a panorama looks wrong, open "Manual control points," mark a few spots on the bad seam, hit "Save and stitch again."
  4. Repeat only for groups that need it.

issues.display_title: Issue #166: load-files shows nothing until the entire directory has been scanned
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.56.33.mov

What happens

msg_load_files builds the complete listing before emitting anything, so the browse grid stays on the previous folder until the last entry has been stat-ed.

src-tauri/src/commands/files.rs — msg_load_files

On fix/nas (commit 6aadddb) this was made much faster: the per-entry metadata() calls now run in parallel via rayon on the blocking pool, and a load-files-start event raises the grid progress bar so the wait is at least visible. But the model is still all-or-nothing — a very large directory on a slow share still shows a progress bar and nothing else for the whole scan.

The progress bar is also necessarily indeterminate, because the entry count is unknown until read_dir finishes. Streaming would make a real 120 / 450 counter possible.

How to reproduce

  1. Mount a network share (SMB) with a directory holding several hundred files.
  2. Open the app, navigate to a different folder first so there is a visible previous listing.
  3. Open the large folder.
  4. The progress bar appears immediately, but the grid keeps showing the old folder contents for the whole scan, then swaps to the complete new listing in one step. Nothing appears incrementally, and the bar gives no sense of how far along it is.

Contrast with recursive search in the same app, which streams results in as they are found.

Goal

The grid fills in progressively instead of waiting for the whole directory, and the progress bar can show a real count.

  • Emit the listing in chunks the way msg_search_recursive already does in the same file — see SEARCH_CHUNK_SIZE / SEARCH_CHUNK_MS (~line 719) and its search-start → search-results → search-done sequence.
  • This touches the renderer: src/renderer/components/core/ipcHandlers/files.ts currently handles load-files as a single payload that replaces the whole list, and sorting happens backend-side across the full set — chunked delivery has to preserve the folders-first ordering.
  • Measure first. After the parallel scan landed, this may no longer be worth the renderer churn.

issues.display_title: Issue #183: Switch product analytics from Aptabase to self-hosted Countly
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Description

Problem: We have no idea how the app is actually being used. The app was supposed to report usage to Aptabase, but the reporting was never actually finished — every event the app tried to send went nowhere. So the analytics dashboard has always been empty, and we've been guessing about which features matter to users.

Solution: Point analytics at our own Countly server (data.gothru.org) instead, and actually finish the wiring so events really get sent.

Countly is self-hosted, so usage data stays on our own server instead of a third party's.

What gets reported:

  • App opens and closes — how many people use the app, how often they come back, and how long a session lasts.
  • Basic environment — operating system and app version, so we can see who's still on an old build.
  • The actions already wired up in the app — switching viewers, changing theme or language, file operations (rename, copy, move, delete, create folder), sorting, bookmarks, uploads, GPS updates, orientation fixes, and app updates.

What is NOT reported: no file names, no folder paths, no image contents, no account details. Each install is identified only by a random ID generated on that machine — it can't be traced back to a person.

Behavior:

  • Only released builds report. Running the app locally during development stays silent, so our own testing doesn't pollute real usage numbers.
  • Analytics never interrupts the user. If the server is unreachable or slow, the app carries on as normal — nothing is shown, nothing is blocked, nothing fails.
  • Closing the app sends one final "session ended" note. If the server doesn't answer, the app waits at most 2 seconds and quits anyway.

Also fixed along the way:

  • Some actions were reporting the same thing under three different spellings, which split one number into three in the dashboard and made it unreadable. Now unified.
  • Changing credentials in the local config file didn't actually take effect until something else changed — the app kept using stale values. This affected Google sign-in settings too, not just analytics.

issues.display_title: Issue #172: Reduce Ram Usage on Stitching Feature
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Description

The Stitching feature (merging multiple photos into a 360 panorama) uses a large amount of RAM while processing, especially with high-resolution source photos or when several images are combined at once. On computers with limited memory (8-16GB), this can slow the whole app down, cause it to freeze, or crash entirely — forcing the user to restart and redo the stitch.

This gets worse as photo resolution and photo count increase, so it's currently a bigger risk for users doing high-quality panorama shoots. Goal: bring RAM usage down so stitching completes reliably without freezing/crashing, even on lower-spec machines.
